a2-results.what: A measured delta, tie-break robustness table or regression sentinel from the A2 pair-level unresolved-origin systematic.
a2-results.why: A2 is a published systematic with a committed pre-registration, and these are the numbers it produced.

anchors-dedup-blocks.what: One directory's species, category and observable tables from the trigger-deduplicating extraction of one tune, central or one canonical block.
anchors-dedup-blocks.why: These eleven directories per tune are the measured input behind the final three-tune table, so a reader checks the published number against them.

anchors-m7-beauty.what: One canonical block's MeasureUnresolvedSystematic log carrying the beauty unresolved and resolved baryon and meson counts.
anchors-m7-beauty.why: It is the committed input that regenerates the published beauty M7 table, the same reproducibility claim the charm blocks carry.

anchors-m7-charm.what: One canonical block's MeasureUnresolvedSystematic log carrying the charm unresolved and resolved baryon and meson counts.
anchors-m7-charm.why: README section 3a rebuilds the published charm M7 table from these logs with extraction/aggregate_m7.py, so they are the check itself.

anchors-replicated-blocks.what: One canonical block's MONASH species table from the pre-E5 replicated extraction, or that set's manifest.
anchors-replicated-blocks.why: The published deduplicated number is defined as the correction of these, so verifying the E5 arithmetic needs both sides.

anchors-sigmab-raw.what: One canonical block's raw Sigma_b ordering log, listing the per-pair counts the asymmetry test consumed.
anchors-sigmab-raw.why: The Sigma_b ordering result is published and these logs are the only committed record of the counts behind it.

attic-split-chain.what: One file of the separate bbbar, ccbar and qqbar production and reduction chain: its producers, its six PYTHIA cards, its reductions and wrappers.
attic-split-chain.why: Owner-ruled 2026-08-20: the export does not carry it, and README section 6 loses the sentence that offered it.

dataset-selectors-systematics.what: The signed dataset selector naming one variation campaign's merged inputs and its publication eligibility.
dataset-selectors-systematics.why: The plotting and harvest chain refuses to run until a dataset is named, and these are the names for the variation campaigns.

extraction-chain.what: One stage of the extraction and systematics chain that turns merged pair output into the published tables and their uncertainties.
extraction-chain.why: This is the code that produces the paper's numbers, so a reader cannot check any of them without it.

harvest-plot-configs.what: The eleven-class three-tune plotting configuration for one variation campaign, generated from the central configuration.
harvest-plot-configs.why: It reproduces one variation's rendered uncertainty matrix, which the systematics combination consumes.

history-audits.what: A previous repository audit or change-justification pass, with its inventory and deletion-candidate lists.
history-audits.why: It is the archaeology of earlier cleanups, and this manifest supersedes it as the current inventory.

history-handoffs.what: One dated handoff in the session chain, written to carry state from one working session to the next.
history-handoffs.why: A handoff records how the work proceeded and nothing a reader needs to rerun the analysis, and the export exclusion names the chain explicitly.

history-other.what: A session transcript, cleanup report, agent working-instruction pack or superseded plotting handoff kept under the history tree.
history-other.why: Each records process rather than method or result, and the export exclusion covers the whole tree.

history-session-records.what: One session's own record of what it did, what it found and what it left open, filed under a dated session name.
history-session-records.why: docs/PUBLICATION_EXPORT_EXCLUSIONS.md excludes docs/history in full: these quote superseded intermediate numbers a reader cannot tell from current ones.

history-studies.what: A superseded standalone study: its macros, its committed numeric outputs and the descriptions of the ROOT files it read.
history-studies.why: These studies ran on older productions and no published number descends from them, so they record how the project got here.

nikhef-cleanup-evidence.what: One record of the executed cluster cleanup: the target list, the pre-removal digests, the per-path manifest or the removal log.
nikhef-cleanup-evidence.why: Owner-ruled 2026-08-20: cluster operations evidence, not a reproduction input.

nikhef-consolidation-records.what: One record of the Nikhef home-directory consolidation: its census, reverse map, resolver pin check or post-acceptance deletion proposal.
nikhef-consolidation-records.why: These files make a cluster administration pass reviewable and reversible; they are not inputs to the physics result.

plotting-configs.what: One plotting configuration naming the objects, classes and display settings for a figure family.
plotting-configs.why: A figure cannot be reproduced without the configuration it was rendered from.

plotting-figure-path.what: One macro, header or helper on the publication figure path, from input validation through projection and styling to the rendered canvas.
plotting-figure-path.why: Every published figure is produced by this code, so a reader checking a figure needs it.

plotting-validation-receipts.what: A figure-render receipt, run record or rendered canvas from one dated plotting validation run, including the variants that were rejected.
plotting-validation-receipts.why: The brief rules boundary receipts PUBLIC: these are how a reader knows a published figure came from the named inputs and command.

systematics-results-final.what: A table, report or machine-readable record from the final systematics combination over the seven variation sources.
systematics-results-final.why: The brief rules docs/systematics_results_* PUBLIC: this is the published uncertainty and the arithmetic behind it.

systematics-results-wave.what: A per-class, per-category, ratio-trend or tune-separation result from an earlier wave of the systematics harvest.
systematics-results-wave.why: The brief rules docs/systematics_results_* PUBLIC, and the final combination is defined relative to these waves.

tests-cpp-contract.what: One compiled C++ contract test asserting a producer or pair-schema invariant that only the real headers can express.
tests-cpp-contract.why: It is part of the same acceptance gate and cannot be dropped without shrinking the denominator make check reports.

tests-fixtures.what: A committed integrated-rows log fixture that a systematics test parses instead of reaching for campaign output.
tests-fixtures.why: Without the fixture its test cannot run, and the test is PUBLIC.

tests-python-contract.what: One standard-library contract test asserting an invariant of the committed source, generated headers, configuration or extraction arithmetic.
tests-python-contract.why: The brief rules tests PUBLIC: the suite is how a reader confirms the checkout is internally consistent before running anything.

tools-chain.what: One campaign-management, generation, validation or rendering tool on the live path between the cards and the published figures.
tools-chain.why: Each is invoked by a documented workflow, a Makefile target or the contract test suite, so rerunning the analysis needs it.

tune-cards-systematics.what: One PYTHIA card for one systematic variation: the nominal tune card with exactly one setting changed.
tune-cards-systematics.why: The published systematic uncertainty is the spread across these cards, so the variation campaigns cannot be regenerated without them.

.gitignore.what: The ignore rules, each annotated with the incident that motivated it, including the rule that keeps the third-party writing standard out of history.
.gitignore.why: A clone needs it to keep build products and campaign scratch out of the tree.

.mailmap.what: Maps seven author identities, including personal and cluster host addresses, onto one canonical contributor.
.mailmap.why: The export is one initial commit with no ancestry, so a mailmap has no history to fold and would only publish the address list.

ARCHITECTURE.md.what: Explains what the repository measures and how the stages connect, written for a physicist who has never used ROOT or PYTHIA.
ARCHITECTURE.md.why: It is the conceptual entry point a reader needs before rerunning anything.

AnalysisScripts/AssociateOriginCategoryC.what: Declares the associate-origin category contract the pair objects are written against.
AnalysisScripts/AssociateOriginCategoryC.why: The category axis of every published decomposition is defined by it.

AnalysisScripts/GeneratedPairObjectContr.what: The generated C++ view of the pair-file object contract, replacing three hand-maintained lists that had drifted apart.
AnalysisScripts/GeneratedPairObjectContr.why: It is a golden output and the closure counts derive from it.

AnalysisScripts/GeneratedPairRegistry.h.what: The generated C++ view of the expanded pair registry, carrying its source digest.
AnalysisScripts/GeneratedPairRegistry.h.why: It is a golden output the analysis, merge and closure all compile against.

AnalysisScripts/GeneratedSpeciesOrdinals.what: The generated C++ view of the species ordinal table, so the ROOT-only analysis needs no JSON parser.
AnalysisScripts/GeneratedSpeciesOrdinals.why: It is a golden output that puts the species axis into the compiled chain.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/MANIFEST.md.what: The index of every anchor directory, naming what each one anchors and whether its provenance is complete or incomplete.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/MANIFEST.md.why: It is the entry point to the provenance chain and states, per anchor, what can be verified and what cannot.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/b4_multiplicity_.what: The manifest of the per-tune minimum-bias N_ch anchor, the evidence behind the multiplicity class definition and figure 3.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/b4_multiplicity_.why: The paper-facing class translation table is recomputed from it rather than transcribed, which is a reproducibility claim.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/b4_multiplicity_.what: The ROOT macro that dumps the minimum-bias N_ch distribution per tune into the committed CSV and ROOT pair.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/b4_multiplicity_.why: It is the committed consumer of the anchor, so the class boundaries can be rederived rather than trusted.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/b4_multiplicity_.what: The CLOSEPACKING minimum-bias charged-multiplicity distribution as text.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/b4_multiplicity_.why: The published multiplicity class boundaries are derived from these distributions, so checking a boundary needs them.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/b4_multiplicity_.what: The CLOSEPACKING minimum-bias charged-multiplicity histogram in ROOT form.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/b4_multiplicity_.why: It is the binary the dump macro reads, and the CSV alone loses the binning the boundaries were cut on.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/b4_multiplicity_.what: The JUNCTIONS minimum-bias charged-multiplicity distribution as text.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/b4_multiplicity_.why: The published multiplicity class boundaries are derived from these distributions, so checking a boundary needs them.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/b4_multiplicity_.what: The JUNCTIONS minimum-bias charged-multiplicity histogram in ROOT form.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/b4_multiplicity_.why: It is the binary the dump macro reads, and the CSV alone loses the binning the boundaries were cut on.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/b4_multiplicity_.what: The MONASH minimum-bias charged-multiplicity distribution as text.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/b4_multiplicity_.why: The published multiplicity class boundaries are derived from these distributions, so checking a boundary needs them.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/b4_multiplicity_.what: The MONASH minimum-bias charged-multiplicity histogram in ROOT form.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/b4_multiplicity_.why: It is the binary the dump macro reads, and the CSV alone loses the binning the boundaries were cut on.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/b4_multiplicity_.what: The run metadata of the minimum-bias generation: card, seed, event count and where it ran.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/b4_multiplicity_.why: It is the provenance line that ties the committed distributions to a specific generator run.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/closure_v3_verdi.what: The manifest of the two closure verdicts that gate the three-tune central table, and where their logs came from.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/closure_v3_verdi.why: The brief rules boundary receipts PUBLIC: this is the record that the published table passed its gate.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/closure_v3_verdi.what: The full CLOSEPACKING pair-block closure run log ending in its CANONICAL_PAIR_BLOCK_CLOSURE_PASS verdict.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/closure_v3_verdi.why: Same role for the third tune's published column.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/closure_v3_verdi.what: The full JUNCTIONS pair-block closure run log ending in the CANONICAL_PAIR_BLOCK_CLOSURE_PASS verdict.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/closure_v3_verdi.why: It is the receipt behind a published column, and it existed only in cluster scratch before it was committed.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/closure_v3_verdi.what: The waiter's own log, showing when each tune's blocks appeared and when each closure started.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/closure_v3_verdi.why: It timestamps the gate runs whose verdicts the published table depends on.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/closure_v3_verdi.what: The polling script that waited for both tunes' blocks to be promoted and then ran the closure gate on each.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/closure_v3_verdi.why: It records how the two committed verdicts were actually produced, which is the invocation half of the receipt.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/closure_v3_verdi.what: The single extracted CLOSEPACKING verdict line, separated from its log.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/closure_v3_verdi.why: Same role for the third tune.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/closure_v3_verdi.what: The single extracted JUNCTIONS verdict line, separated from its log.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/closure_v3_verdi.why: It is the quotable form of the gate result the central table cites.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/e5fix_drivers/MA.what: The manifest of the drivers that produced the JUNCTIONS and CLOSEPACKING columns and the MONASH E5 re-extraction.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/e5fix_drivers/MA.why: It names the exact invocation behind published columns, which the tracked extractor alone does not record.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/e5fix_drivers/ru.what: The driver that ran the deduplicating extractor over all ten canonical blocks of one tune.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/e5fix_drivers/ru.why: It is the recorded invocation behind the committed per-block tables.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/e5fix_drivers/ru.what: The driver that ran the deduplicating extractor over one tune's central merged directory.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/e5fix_drivers/ru.why: Same reason: the central column's invocation is part of its provenance.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/e5fix_drivers/ru.what: The driver that assembled the three-tune table from the per-tune extractions.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/e5fix_drivers/ru.why: It is how the published table was generated, and the table is the resubmission's central number.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/e5fix_drivers/ve.what: The check that the deduplicated extraction reproduces the predicted E5 totals rather than merely differing from the replicated one.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/e5fix_drivers/ve.why: It is the positive check that turned the E5 correction from an assertion into a measurement.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/extraction_dual/.what: The manifest of the first anchor extraction, carrying the quarantine notice that forbids its weights for charge-resolved use.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/extraction_dual/.why: The quarantine is a correctness warning attached to numbers that several published documents were computed from, so it travels with them.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/extraction_dual/.what: The per-category weights of the quarantined first anchor extraction.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/extraction_dual/.why: It is the category-level half of the anchor whose defect the published E4 comparison reports.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/extraction_dual/.what: The per-observable weights of the quarantined first anchor extraction.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/extraction_dual/.why: It completes the anchor that decay-map v2 weighting and the E4 comparison both read.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/extraction_dual/.what: The per-species weights of the quarantined first anchor extraction.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/extraction_dual/.why: README section 3a feeds it to compare_subset_parent.py to reproduce the E4 anchor defect, which is a published finding.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/f4_probe/build_r.what: The build and run manifest of the extended probe, with the digests of the binary and its inputs.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/f4_probe/build_r.why: It is how a reader ties the committed probe output to the code that produced it.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/f4_probe/f4_prob.what: The original PYTHIA-linked decay probe output: 202 species, dominant channel only.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/f4_probe/f4_prob.why: README section 3a rebuilds decay map v1.1 from this file and checks the digest, which is one of the two headline reproduction checks.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/f4_probe/f4b_pro.what: The extended decay probe output carrying 5,576 F4_CHANNEL lines, every channel rather than the dominant one.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/f4_probe/f4b_pro.why: Decay map v2 rebuilds from it, and its byte-identical F4_SPECIES lines are the evidence that the probe was extended rather than changed.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/f4_probe/pdgs.tx.what: The list of 202 species codes the decay probe was asked to resolve.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/f4_probe/pdgs.tx.why: It is the probe's input, so the map rebuild is not reproducible without it.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/merged_closepack.what: The manifest of the CLOSEPACKING deduplicated extraction, recording the run, its inputs and the E5 checks it was made to settle.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/merged_closepack.why: It states what the tune's committed tables mean and which prediction they were scored against.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/merged_junctions.what: The manifest of the JUNCTIONS deduplicated extraction, recording the run, its inputs and the E5 checks it was made to settle.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/merged_junctions.why: It states what the tune's committed tables mean and which prediction they were scored against.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/merged_monash_de.what: The manifest of the MONASH deduplicated extraction, recording the run, its inputs and the E5 checks it was made to settle.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/merged_monash_de.why: It states what the tune's committed tables mean and which prediction they were scored against.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/merged_monash_re.what: The MONASH per-category table from the same replicated, pre-E5 extraction.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/merged_monash_re.why: It is the category-level parent for that published comparison.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/merged_monash_re.what: The same MONASH per-category table after the E5 trigger deduplication.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/merged_monash_re.why: Same role at category level: it is how the published correction is verified.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/merged_monash_re.what: The MONASH per-species table from the REPLICATED, pre-E5 extraction, the parent the anchor comparison is run against.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/merged_monash_re.why: README section 3a names it as the parent input to the E4 anchor-versus-parent comparison, which is a published finding.

AnalysisScripts/anchors/merged_monash_re.what: The same MONASH per-species table after the E5 trigger deduplication was applied by arithmetic inversion.
AnalysisScripts/anchors/merged_monash_re.why: It bridges the replicated anchor to the final table, and the published E5 correction is checked against it.

AnalysisScripts/decay_parent_map_v1.json.what: The original decay-parent map, which does not conjugate antiparticle decays and is the artifact behind the conjugation bug.
AnalysisScripts/decay_parent_map_v1.json.why: Owner-ruled 2026-08-20: a known-defective artifact is a reproduction hazard in a reader's hands, and MAP_V1_CONJUGATION_BUG carries the evidence without shipping the file.

AnalysisScripts/decay_parent_map_v1_1.js.what: The decay-parent map with the conjugation fix applied, chaining each species through its dominant channel.
AnalysisScripts/decay_parent_map_v1_1.js.why: It is a golden output, README rebuilds it from committed inputs, and the published extraction names it explicitly.

AnalysisScripts/decay_parent_map_v2.json.what: The species-level decay-parent map with fractional branching-ratio splits.
AnalysisScripts/decay_parent_map_v2.json.why: It is a golden output and the experiment-comparable convention uses it.

AnalysisScripts/species_ordinals_v2.json.what: The derived 202-entry sector-charged species ordinal table, the spine the species axis is indexed by.
AnalysisScripts/species_ordinals_v2.json.why: It is a golden output and every per-species number is addressed through it.

Literature/References.bib.what: The BibTeX database of works the project cites.
Literature/References.bib.why: A reader following the physics needs the citations, and a bibliography carries no third-party content.

Literature/pveen_14443260_msc_thesis-1_m.what: A 2 MB PDF of another author's MSc thesis, the predecessor work this project builds on.
Literature/pveen_14443260_msc_thesis-1_m.why: Owner-ruled 2026-08-20: the export cites the thesis and drops the file, on the same reasoning as the ASD-STE100 exclusion.

Makefile.what: The top-level driver: setup, doctor, build, card and registry checks, the test suite, submission targets and the environment verdict.
Makefile.why: It is the entry point every documented workflow starts from.

POST_SUBMISSION.md.what: The parked-work list: everything deliberately deferred until after submission, with the rule that nothing on it blocks the paper.
POST_SUBMISSION.md.why: It is a work queue for the authors and states itself that no paper claim depends on any of it.

Paper/Tables/generated_heavy_flavor_summ.what: The generated LaTeX table of per-tune event counts and inclusive species yields that the manuscript includes.
Paper/Tables/generated_heavy_flavor_summ.why: Owner-ruled 2026-08-20: the manuscript is untracked and A9 records these numbers as descending from a superseded production.

README.md.what: The rebuild guide, ordered by what a reader would actually do from nothing, with the smoke path and the list of what is not evidence.
README.md.why: It is the primary instruction for rerunning the analysis.

RELEASE_BLOCKERS.md.what: The closed list of remaining scope before release, every row citing a path, line or digest and its run status.
RELEASE_BLOCKERS.md.why: It is project management for the authors: it tracks what is left to do, not how to rerun or check anything.

RENAMES.md.what: Records what the 2026-08-12 restructure moved, what it deliberately did not move, and the owner overrides that struck rows.
RENAMES.md.why: The export is a fresh single commit with no prior paths, so a record of moves out of an older layout has nothing to refer to.

REPRODUCIBILITY.md.what: States what must be true for a number from this repository to be reproducible, and how each contract, selector, threshold and pin is enforced.
REPRODUCIBILITY.md.why: It is the physics contract a reader checks a published number against.

STATE.md.what: The one-screen answer to where the project stands: what is frozen, what is pending, what is written but unrun, and what is not planned.
STATE.md.why: It tells a reader which numbers are final and which are provisional, which is a precondition for checking any of them.

Validation/AuditOriginResolution.C.what: Audits how heavy-flavour origins resolved in a raw file: unresolved, resolved, demoted and rejected candidates.
Validation/AuditOriginResolution.C.why: The unresolved-origin systematic is computed from exactly this accounting.

Validation/AuditSpeciesRegistry.C.what: Audits the signed species registry against the linked PYTHIA's own particle data.
Validation/AuditSpeciesRegistry.C.why: It is how the registry is shown to agree with the generator that produced the data.

Validation/AuditTuneSettings.C.what: Audits a produced file's recorded tune settings against the generated tune registry.
Validation/AuditTuneSettings.C.why: It is how a reader confirms a data file was made with the card it claims.

Validation/CalibrateBothCountersAgainstM.what: The two-counter variant of that calibration, comparing both charged-multiplicity definitions against the same reference.
Validation/CalibrateBothCountersAgainstM.why: It answers which counter definition a class boundary refers to, which a reader comparing to data needs.

Validation/CalibrateMultiplicityAgainstM.what: Calibrates the charged-multiplicity counter against a published minimum-bias reference.
Validation/CalibrateMultiplicityAgainstM.why: Three validation reports are its recorded output and the multiplicity classes are cut on the counter it calibrates.

Validation/CompareNominalReproduction.C.what: Asks whether a rebuilt producer reproduces the nominal output file, as pre-registered.
Validation/CompareNominalReproduction.C.why: It is the check a third party runs after building PYTHIA themselves, which README names as the project's largest portability limitation.

Validation/ListUnresolvedOrigins.C.what: Lists the individual unresolved-origin candidates rather than counting them.
Validation/ListUnresolvedOrigins.C.why: It is how a reader inspects the cases behind the published systematic.

Validation/MeasureUnresolvedSystematic.C.what: Measures the systematic from dropping unresolved candidates, per sector.
Validation/MeasureUnresolvedSystematic.C.why: It produced the committed M7 charm and beauty block logs the published tables aggregate.

Validation/PTHatSensitivity.C.what: Extracts the predeclared pTHat sensitivity test from its immutable manifest and decides it.
Validation/PTHatSensitivity.C.why: The published pTHat threshold rests on this test's verdict.

Validation/TestAnalysisRawInputContract..what: Compiles the reduction against a raw file and asserts the input contract holds.
Validation/TestAnalysisRawInputContract..why: A test in the PUBLIC suite compiles it, so the suite needs it.

Validation/TestHardCarrierUniqueness.C.what: Asserts that a hard carrier resolves uniquely under the shared helper.
Validation/TestHardCarrierUniqueness.C.why: Hard-carrier uniqueness is an assumption of the observable, and this is the only file that tests it.

Validation/TestInclusiveRawKinematics.C.what: Compiles the inclusive kinematic spectra macro and asserts its raw-level kinematics.
Validation/TestInclusiveRawKinematics.C.why: It bears on the inclusive spectra blocker, so it answers a question a referee can ask.

Validation/TestPlotProjectionCuts.C.what: Asserts that the plotting macro's projection cuts select the intended sparse ranges.
Validation/TestPlotProjectionCuts.C.why: It checks the cuts behind every published figure, and the census argues explicitly against sweeping unrun validators away.

Validation/TestPlotReferenceMultiplicity.what: Asserts the plotting macro's reference-multiplicity contracts inside a memory file.
Validation/TestPlotReferenceMultiplicity.why: A test in the PUBLIC suite compiles it.

Validation/TestPrimaryChargedDefinition..what: Asserts two claims about the primary-charged definition against the installed PYTHIA rather than against fixtures.
Validation/TestPrimaryChargedDefinition..why: The primary-charged definition is what the multiplicity classes count, so its live-generator check is reader-facing.

Validation/ValidateCanonicalRawManifest..what: Validates every raw file named by a canonical manifest, reusing the raw validator.
Validation/ValidateCanonicalRawManifest..why: It is how a whole campaign's inputs are certified before the merge.

Validation/ValidatePairBlockClosure.C.what: The closure gate: checks the central against its blocks and returns the content and invariant counts.
Validation/ValidatePairBlockClosure.C.why: It is the check that a merge is complete, and the brief rules boundary receipts PUBLIC.

Validation/ValidatePairDirectory.C.what: Checks a completed pair directory against the pair registry and the object contract, name by name.
Validation/ValidatePairDirectory.C.why: The reduction promotes a directory only if this passes, so it defines a valid analysis output.

Validation/ValidateRawOutput.C.what: Validates one produced raw file against the canonical schema and emits the origin audit the receipt records.
Validation/ValidateRawOutput.C.why: It is the gate every raw file passes before it may be analysed.

Validation/ValidateSpeciesAxisClosure.C.what: Checks the 202-ordinal species axis against the six-bin category axis it refines, exactly.
Validation/ValidateSpeciesAxisClosure.C.why: SPECIES_AXIS_VALIDATION is its record and the species axis carries the published decomposition.

Validation/validate_canonical_manifest.s.what: Drives that manifest validation over a campaign.
Validation/validate_canonical_manifest.s.why: It is the entry point for the campaign-scale input gate.

Validation/validate_pair_block_closure.s.what: Resolves the requested schema tag and runs the closure gate, rejecting an unknown schema before ROOT starts.
Validation/validate_pair_block_closure.s.why: The published three-tune table is gated on this script's verdict.

Validation/validate_pair_directory.sh.what: The wrapper the reduction calls to validate a staged pair directory.
Validation/validate_pair_directory.sh.why: README's smoke path names it as the validation step.

Validation/validate_raw_output.sh.what: Runs that raw validator and writes the receipt beside the file.
Validation/validate_raw_output.sh.why: The receipt is the evidence a raw file is usable, and this writes it.

ValidationReports/NCH_CALIBRATION_202607.what: Calibrates the charged-multiplicity counter against a published minimum-bias reference under PYTHIA 8.315.
ValidationReports/NCH_CALIBRATION_202607.why: It is the first calibration of the counter the multiplicity classes are cut on, and later reports are stated as supersessions of it.

ValidationReports/NCH_CALIBRATION_PYTHIA.what: Repeats that calibration under the pinned stock PYTHIA 8.317 and supersedes the 8.315 result.
ValidationReports/NCH_CALIBRATION_PYTHIA.why: It is the calibration at the version the published production actually ran.

ValidationReports/NCH_DECAY_POLICY_BIAS_.what: Re-measures the bias the decay policy puts on the charged-multiplicity count at the pinned version.
ValidationReports/NCH_DECAY_POLICY_BIAS_.why: It corrects a figure quoted in the design rationale, so a reader checking the class definition needs it.

ValidationReports/PREPRODUCTION_GATE_REP.what: The human-readable evidence ledger for the pre-production gate, concluding that full production was not authorized at that date.
ValidationReports/PREPRODUCTION_GATE_REP.why: It is an authorization decision at a superseded state of the project.

ValidationReports/PTHAT_MULTIPLICITY_SCA.what: Scans the hard sample's charged multiplicity against the pTHat minimum at the pinned version.
ValidationReports/PTHAT_MULTIPLICITY_SCA.why: REPRODUCIBILITY section 1 cites it as the evidence for the pTHat threshold the production uses.

ValidationReports/PYTHIA_JUNCTION_HANG_2.what: Records the PYTHIA junction-splitting infinite loop found in a pilot campaign, with the configuration that triggers it.
ValidationReports/PYTHIA_JUNCTION_HANG_2.why: The hang guard and the non-random event loss it causes are stated in README, and this is the measurement behind that statement.

docs/a2_evidence_20260813/regression_sen.what: The A2 regression sentinel written by the comparison tool itself rather than transcribed.
docs/a2_evidence_20260813/regression_sen.why: It is the machine-checkable evidence that the A2 variation reproduced its baseline before its delta was used.

docs/a2_evidence_20260813/slot_0_5478114.what: One A2 job slot's standard error stream, kept from the queued run.
docs/a2_evidence_20260813/slot_0_5478114.why: It is a single job's error log from one campaign, not evidence for a published quantity.

docs/a2_regression_pass_permissive_large.what: The machine-readable A2 regression verdict for the largest-index tie-break variation.
docs/a2_regression_pass_permissive_large.why: It is the sentinel that records whether the A2 variation reproduced its baseline, which the published systematic depends on.

docs/a2_regression_pass_permissive_small.what: The same regression verdict for the pre-registered smallest-index tie-break.
docs/a2_regression_pass_permissive_small.why: It is the sentinel for the tie-break the A2 pre-registration actually selected.

docs/campaigns/HF_RUN3_V1_PARTIALS_ARCHI.what: The manifest of 34 partial staging directories moved out of the gate's scan root, recorded so the move is reversible.
docs/campaigns/HF_RUN3_V1_PARTIALS_ARCHI.why: It documents a reversible housekeeping action on cluster storage.

docs/campaigns/HF_RUN3_V1_RECORD.md.what: The campaign record for the production behind the published dataset: what was rendered, when it was submitted and when it was released.
docs/campaigns/HF_RUN3_V1_RECORD.md.why: It is the provenance of the events every published number is computed from.

docs/history/studies/Balancing_and_Sampl.what: Warns that double-counting is not implemented from 23 December onward and that results from this directory need dividing by two, ending with the note that this remains to be checked.
docs/history/studies/Balancing_and_Sampl.why: It is an unresolved caveat on a superseded study, ruled out of scope only while no published number descends from that directory.

docs/history/studies/Balancing_and_Sampl.what: The macro whose double-counting logic decides whether the factor of two in ATTENTION.txt applies to any quoted number.
docs/history/studies/Balancing_and_Sampl.why: It is the file to read if the caveat reopens, and the census names it for exactly that, but no current figure depends on it.

docs/writing_standard/STANDARD.md.what: The repository's writing standard: the Simplified Technical English and Orwell rules every tracked document is written against.
docs/writing_standard/STANDARD.md.why: Owner-ruled 2026-08-20: the writing standard does not travel.

docs/writing_standard/pdf-page-map.md.what: Maps the repository's rule numbering onto pages of the third-party ASD-STE100 specification, which is deliberately untracked.
docs/writing_standard/pdf-page-map.md.why: It indexes into a copyrighted document that the export cannot carry, and the exclusions list already forbids redistributing it.

docs/writing_standard/ste-rules.md.what: The rule-by-rule reference behind that standard, in the repository's own wording.
docs/writing_standard/ste-rules.md.why: Owner-ruled 2026-08-20: it stays with the standard it expands.

extraction/aggregate_m7.py.what: Aggregates the unresolved-origin systematic across the ten canonical blocks, per sector.
extraction/aggregate_m7.py.why: README section 3a runs it on committed logs to reproduce a published table.

extraction/compare_subset_parent.py.what: Compares a per-species subset table against the parent it was drawn from, under an explicitly named null.
extraction/compare_subset_parent.py.why: It is the mechanism behind the published anchor defect, and the null has no default because the choice changes the verdict.

extraction/decompose_with_block_sems.py.what: Produces the species decomposition with block standard errors in both conventions, using the pre-registered estimator.
extraction/decompose_with_block_sems.py.why: The published central values and their uncertainties come from it.

extraction/extract_species_decomposition.what: Projects a merged directory's 202-bin species closure and groups it by category, with the decay map named explicitly.
extraction/extract_species_decomposition.why: It is the first extraction layer over merged output and the source of every per-species table.

extraction/three_tune_table.py.what: Builds the three-tune table on a common row set so the columns are comparable, in both conventions.
extraction/three_tune_table.py.why: It generates the resubmission's central table.

extraction/write_verdict.py.what: Decides whether the tune separation exceeds its total uncertainty, computing the systematic on the separation rather than borrowing one.
extraction/write_verdict.py.why: It renders the paper's headline verdict.

generation/Simulation_README.md.what: Explains the producer, its cards and how a generation job is run.
generation/Simulation_README.md.why: It is the subsystem guide for the first pipeline stage.

generation/cards/pythiasettings_Hard_Low.what: The CLOSEPACKING PYTHIA card, one of the three published tunes.
generation/cards/pythiasettings_Hard_Low.why: The published comparison is between exactly these three cards.

generation/cards/pythiasettings_Hard_Low.what: The JUNCTIONS PYTHIA card, one of the three published tunes.
generation/cards/pythiasettings_Hard_Low.why: The published comparison is between exactly these three cards.

generation/cards/pythiasettings_Hard_Low.what: A fourth JUNCTIONS card with matched settings, deliberately outside the published tune set.
generation/cards/pythiasettings_Hard_Low.why: It is a documented reference point, and its exclusion from the published set is itself a recorded contract the registry depends on.

generation/cards/pythiasettings_Hard_Low.what: The MONASH PYTHIA card, one of the three published tunes.
generation/cards/pythiasettings_Hard_Low.why: The published comparison is between exactly these three cards.

generation/producer/HeavyFlavourUtils.h.what: The shared heavy-flavour helpers: species classification, hard-carrier resolution and the charged-multiplicity counter.
generation/producer/HeavyFlavourUtils.h.why: Producer, validators and analysis all include it, so its definitions are the observable's definitions.

generation/producer/Makefile.what: Builds the producer against the pinned PYTHIA and ROOT.
generation/producer/Makefile.why: It is the documented build path for the generation stage.

generation/producer/Sha256.h.what: A self-contained SHA-256 implementation used to stamp inputs and outputs inside ROOT and PYTHIA code.
generation/producer/Sha256.h.why: The provenance digests a reader verifies are computed with it.

generation/producer/heavyflavourcorrelat.what: The PYTHIA producer: generates events and writes the canonical raw schema with its heavy-flavour audit trees.
generation/producer/heavyflavourcorrelat.why: It is the stage that makes the data, so nothing can be rerun without it.

generation/registries/GeneratedHeavyFlav.what: The generated C++ view of the signed species registry, carrying the source digest.
generation/registries/GeneratedHeavyFlav.why: It is a golden output and the compiled code reads the registry only through it.

generation/registries/GeneratedTuneSetti.what: The generated C++ view of the tune settings the producer records per run.
generation/registries/GeneratedTuneSetti.why: It is a golden output that ties a produced file to the card that made it.

generation/run_hf.sh.what: Runs the producer for one tune and job outside the batch system.
generation/run_hf.sh.why: It is the local entry point for generating events.

generation/submit/Condor_README.md.what: The cluster operations guide: submitting, monitoring, the hang guard and the retry path.
generation/submit/Condor_README.md.why: README names it as the owner of cluster operations, which rerunning the production requires.

generation/submit/runCondorJob.sh.what: The worker script each production job runs: sets up the environment, runs the producer under the wall-clock guard, and writes the sidecar.
generation/submit/runCondorJob.sh.why: It is the job body behind all 3000 production files.

generation/submit/submit_status_analysis.what: Submits the analysis stage over a rendered manifest.
generation/submit/submit_status_analysis.why: It is the documented entry point to the reduction stage on a cluster.

merging/MergeAnalysisObjects.C.what: Object-level merger for status-analysis outputs, safer than a blind file merge because it merges known objects only.
merging/MergeAnalysisObjects.C.why: The canonical merge includes it, and the object list is part of the closure contract.

merging/MergeCanonicalAnalysis.C.what: Merges a canonical set of per-job pair directories into one directory, registry-aware.
merging/MergeCanonicalAnalysis.C.why: It is the macro the merge driver calls, so the merged product is defined by it.

merging/make_subsamples.sh.what: Builds the subsample files the transverse-momentum figures are drawn from.
merging/make_subsamples.sh.why: Those figures cannot be regenerated without their subsample inputs.

merging/merge_root_files.sh.what: The merge driver: builds the three centrals and the thirty blocks, refusing to start without an explicit pair schema.
merging/merge_root_files.sh.why: It is the stage that produces the merged product every published number is extracted from.

plotting/FinalAnalysis/README.md.what: Explains the two remaining macros in the FinalAnalysis directory and their scheduled retirement.
plotting/FinalAnalysis/README.md.why: Both macros are still invoked by the figure driver, so a reader running it meets them.

plotting/GeneratedClassLabelPrecision.h.what: The generated header carrying the multiplicity class label precision, derived from the single boundary source.
plotting/GeneratedClassLabelPrecision.h.why: It is a generated artifact the figures compile against, so the labels cannot drift from the boundaries.

plotting/PAPER_FIGURE_PROVENANCE.md.what: Maps the manuscript's figures to the generators that reproduce them.
plotting/PAPER_FIGURE_PROVENANCE.md.why: It is the figure-to-code provenance a reader follows from a published figure back to its command.

plotting/PtMultiplicity/README.md.what: Explains the subsample transverse-momentum and ratio figures and how their combined input file is built.
plotting/PtMultiplicity/README.md.why: It is the guide to a published figure family.

plotting/README.md.what: Explains the publication plotting path, its fail-closed input selection and the full and reduced configurations.
plotting/README.md.why: It is the subsystem guide for the figure stage.

plotting/improvedPlotting_THnSparse.C.what: The main sparse-histogram plotting macro: reads the merged product, projects the selected ranges and emits the balancing canvases.
plotting/improvedPlotting_THnSparse.C.why: It renders the paper's central figures and its uncertainty matrix feeds the systematics harvest.

plotting/paper/README.md.what: States that every paper figure is generated from committed tables by script, with no hand steps.
plotting/paper/README.md.why: It is the guide to the figure layer that carries the strongest reproducibility claim in the repository.

plotting/paper/figures/fig1_species_deco.what: The committed rendered figure for the species decomposition.
plotting/paper/figures/fig1_species_deco.why: It is a published figure and its committed bytes are what the generator is checked to reproduce.

plotting/paper/figures/fig2_m7_inclusive.what: The committed rendered figure for the inclusive unresolved-origin shift.
plotting/paper/figures/fig2_m7_inclusive.why: It is a published figure and its committed bytes are what the generator is checked to reproduce.

plotting/paper/figures/fig3_multiplicity.what: The committed rendered figure for the multiplicity class definition.
plotting/paper/figures/fig3_multiplicity.why: It is a published figure and its committed bytes are what the generator is checked to reproduce.

plotting/paper/make_paper_figures.py.what: Generates the paper figures from committed tables, with no hand step and no number that exists only inside a figure.
plotting/paper/make_paper_figures.py.why: It is how the published figures are rebuilt from committed inputs.

plotting/paper/svgkit.py.what: A dependency-free byte-deterministic SVG writer used by the figure generator.
plotting/paper/svgkit.py.why: Byte determinism is what lets the committed figures carry digests.

plotting/run_paper_plots.sh.what: The figure driver: names the five paper macros and refuses to run until a dataset is named.
plotting/run_paper_plots.sh.why: It is the entry point that turns merged output into the published figures.

setupEnv.sh.what: Asserts the pinned ROOT and PYTHIA versions and exports nothing on a mismatch, so environment drift cannot reach a number.
setupEnv.sh.why: Every documented command sources it first.

tests/test_prose_check_ing_start.py.what: Pins the writing checker's -ing-start stoplist so a bare imperative verb whose stem ends in -ing does not flag.
tests/test_prose_check_ing_start.py.why: Owner-ruled 2026-08-20: it tests a tool the export does not carry, so shipping it would leave the suite naming a file that is not there.

tests/test_public_never_cites_internal.p.what: Rebuilds the PUBLIC-cites-INTERNAL scan and fails on any reference the committed citation ledger does not already record.
tests/test_public_never_cites_internal.p.why: It reads the manifest and the ledger, both INTERNAL, and it enforces a rule about an export that has not been built yet.

tests/test_repo_audit_manifest.py.what: Asserts the manifest covers exactly the tracked path set, round-trips through the csv module and carries no invalid class.
tests/test_repo_audit_manifest.py.why: Its class was wrong: it opens docs/REPO_AUDIT.csv, so publishing it would ship a test that names a file the export excludes.

tests/test_terms_registry.py.what: Fails on any ruled-out term the committed baseline does not already record, and checks that every registry row is complete.
tests/test_terms_registry.py.why: It reads the baseline and the registry parser, both INTERNAL, so shipping it would leave the suite naming files the export excludes.

tools/GenerateSpeciesOrdinals.C.what: Derives the sector-charged species ordinal table from a produced file's stability audit tree.
tools/GenerateSpeciesOrdinals.C.why: It generates the species ordinal artifact that the whole decomposition is indexed by.

tools/archive_breach_partials.sh.what: Moves provably superseded partial staging directories out of the gate's scan root and writes a manifest of what moved.
tools/archive_breach_partials.sh.why: It is a one-shot housekeeping action on cluster storage whose single run is already recorded in a campaign manifest.

tools/build_producer.sh.what: Builds the producer through the Makefile with the pinned toolchain.
tools/build_producer.sh.why: It is the documented build step.

tools/checkout_advance_guard.py.what: Refuses to advance the analysis checkout while jobs pinned to the current commit are still in flight.
tools/checkout_advance_guard.py.why: A test in the PUBLIC suite exercises it, and the invariant it protects applies to any cluster the chain runs on.

tools/docs_check.sh.what: Prints which owning document corresponds to the paths changed since the last commit, advisory only and never failing.
tools/docs_check.sh.why: It supports the documented rule that a code change and its documentation change land together.

tools/doctor.sh.what: Reports what the current machine can and cannot do, without ever failing.
tools/doctor.sh.why: It is the first command a new machine runs.

tools/environment_verdict.sh.what: Ends make check with an explicit environment verdict and fails on an off-pin runtime unless the run is declared unpinned.
tools/environment_verdict.sh.why: It closes the defect where a machine that cannot run the pipeline reported the greenest check.

tools/f4_probe.cc.what: The decay-parent probe, compiled against the pinned PYTHIA, whose output the decay maps are built from.
tools/f4_probe.cc.why: The committed probe output is a golden input and this is the only code that can regenerate it.

tools/harvest_launch_merge.sh.what: Launches one variation merge behind six refusals, a pipeline lock and a full identity record.
tools/harvest_launch_merge.sh.why: Every published systematic variation was merged through it.

tools/install_checkout_guard_hook.sh.what: Installs that guard as a git hook on a clone that runs jobs.
tools/install_checkout_guard_hook.sh.why: It is how the guard is actually put in force on a running checkout.

tools/merge_supervisor.sh.what: Supervises the canonical merge: detects death, re-runs the pre-checks and restarts it.
tools/merge_supervisor.sh.why: The merge is the longest stage in the chain and this is how a rerun survives it.

tools/prose_check.py.what: Applies the mechanical subset of the repository's writing rules to a document and flags sentences to look at.
tools/prose_check.py.why: Owner-ruled 2026-08-20: the standard does not travel and that covers its checker, so the tool leaves with the rules it enforces.

tools/repo_audit.py.what: Measures size, last-commit date, reference count and entry-point membership for every tracked path, then writes the audit manifest and its citation ledger.
tools/repo_audit.py.why: Its class was wrong: it reads the rulings file and writes the manifest, both INTERNAL, so it exists to serve a decision the export does not carry.

tools/repo_audit_rulings.json.what: The hand-written publication rulings the manifest is built from, keyed by path and by group.
tools/repo_audit_rulings.json.why: It is the working input to an internal decision about what to publish.

tools/run_tests.sh.what: Runs the Python contract tests by glob and states plainly that a run without ROOT is smaller rather than green.
tools/run_tests.sh.why: It is the suite's entry point and the warning it prints is part of reading a result correctly.

tools/supervisor_eol_watch.sh.what: Stops the merge supervisor only once the merge has completed cleanly.
tools/supervisor_eol_watch.sh.why: It closes the supervisor loop the merge stage depends on.

tools/terms_check.py.what: Scans PUBLIC prose for the terms the registry rules out and maintains the baseline of violations that already exist.
tools/terms_check.py.why: It reads the audit manifest to find PUBLIC files and writes an INTERNAL baseline, so it serves a decision the export does not carry.
